chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'ammara ibn Khallad, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about prostrating on snow, so he said, 'Do not prostrate in the salt flat, nor on the snow.'

Because this report is understood to apply in the case of choice (when one has the option to place a covering), or when there is something with which the snow is covered and one prostrates upon it, as we clarified in the report of Mansur ibn Hazim.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to prostrate directly on snow during prayer?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), clarifying that the prohibition against prostrating directly on snow or salt flats (sabbakha) is not absolute but conditional upon the presence of a suitable covering or the ability to choose one. This interpretation aligns with the principle of *al-khbar al-mahmul ala al-ikhtiyar* (the report assumed to apply when one has the choice), ensuring that the ground remains pure and distinct from the worshipper, as further elucidated in the narration of Mansur ibn Hazim.
